title: Define audit event schema and structured-change-record (SCR) for admin actions
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Goal: produce a final, backwards-compatible audit event schema and a compact, privacy-preserving change encoding (named Structured Change Record, SCR) tailored to admin and RBAC v2 events (user/role changes, SSO/SAML config updates, token/key lifecycle, permission grants/revokes).

Motivation and constraints:
- Audit logs must be machine-consumable for alerting and downstream analytics, and human-readable for forensics.
- Must capture actor, target, intent, outcome, and a compact diff for configuration edits without leaking sensitive values (secrets, PII).
- Schema must be stable across hosted/dedicated/private deployments; include versioning to allow evolution.
- Minimize event size for high-throughput control-plane operations; allow optional full payload when requested by a retention/forensics workflow.

Proposed shape (top-level fields):
- schema_version: string (e.g., "audit.v1")
- event_id: string (UUIDv4)
- occurred_at: RFC3339 timestamp
- source: string (component, e.g., "console", "admin-api", "saml-provider")
- event_type: string (categorical, see taxonomy list below)
- actor: string (canonical actor id; prefixed by type, e.g., "user:ashakapoor", "service:deploy-bot")
- actor_type: string (one of: user, service, system, external_idp)
- target: string (canonical target id; prefixed by type, e.g., "org:rwf", "role:admin", "key:kj12...")
- target_type: string (one of: org, project, user, role, token, key, config)
- action: string (imperative verb e.g., "create_role", "update_saml_config", "revoke_token")
- outcome: string (success | failure | partial)
- outcome_detail: optional string (human-friendly explanation or error code)
- scrubbed: string (true|false) - indicates whether values were redacted
- metadata: optional freeform string for short context (e.g., request_id, latency_ms)
- change: optional string or SCR wrapper (see below)
- references: optional list of strings (URLs to PRs, dashboards, runbooks)

Taxonomy guidance (non-exhaustive):
- Administrative config: create_role, update_role, delete_role, assign_role, remove_role
- Identity provider: saml_create, saml_update, saml_delete, idp_provision
- Keys/tokens: create_key, rotate_key, revoke_key, create_token, revoke_token
- System/operation: upgrade_start, upgrade_complete, emergency_failover
- Access control decisions should be logged as separate events (authorize_check, authorize_denied) when they are relevant to troubleshooting.

Structured Change Record (SCR) rationale and design:
- Many admin events are config edits. We need a compact, deterministic, and privacy-aware diff encoding that supports partial values, large objects, and repeated field edits.
- We propose SCR: a small array of operations with canonical ordering; each op is represented as a compact colon-delimited tuple encoded as a single string to keep event size low. SCR ops are NOT nested JSON in the log entry but canonical tokens so indexing and text-search remain efficient.

SCR op format (string): "op|path|before_hash|after_hash|human_hint"
- op: one-letter operation: A (add), R (remove), M (modify)
- path: JSONPath-like dotted path (e.g., "saml.assertion_consumer.url")
- before_hash / after_hash: truncated sha256 hex (8 chars) of the value when available; use "<redacted>" for sensitive fields or when value omitted
- human_hint: short human-visible string (max 80 chars) to summarize change, used for quick inspection and alert templates. Must be plain ASCII.

Example SCR array serialized as JSON string in the change field:
- change: "[\"M|saml.entity_id|9f2a1b3c|a7d4e8f0|updated-entity-id\", \"R|config.legacy_flag|c3d2b1a0|<redacted>|removed-legacy-flag\"]"

Rules for redaction and hashing:
- Fields marked in the sensitive field registry (secrets, certs, private keys, assertion XMLs, personal emails) must never appear in plaintext. Replace with "<redacted>" for before/after and set scrubbed=true.
- For non-sensitive but large fields, include only the 8-char hash and optionally a truncated human_hint.
- Hash use is to enable deterministic correlation without exposing values. Document hashing algorithm and truncation in the runtime-1.20 release notes.

Event size & guarantees:
- If SCR length > 2KiB or number of ops > 100, attach a pointer in references to the full artifact stored in the secure evidence store with a short-lived URL (expires) and a signed manifest id.
- For private deployments where evidence store is disabled, the SCR should fall back to summarization op: "S|summary|<redacted>|<redacted>|long-change-summarized".

Indexing, querying and analytics:
- Provide derived fields for common queries: event_type, actor, target, outcome, changed_paths (a small list of top-3 dotted paths) to enable performant searches without parsing SCR.
- The change field remains freeform but with a recommended standard for ops so that parsers can reconstruct useful deltas.

Compatibility & rollout plan:
- Implement auditor-side library that emits audit.v1. It will include a feature-flag to emit legacy "diff_blob" for a transitional period.
- Backwards compatibility: include mappings from existing event shapes (ENG-9021) during ingestion for 6 months.

Privacy and compliance considerations:
- We will not log secrets/cert contents. Keys/tokens events should record key IDs and fingerprints only.
- For EU customers, provide configuration to disable SCR hashing and instead send minimal events or keep logs on-prem.

Open questions / trade-offs:
1) Use JSON-Patch (RFC6902) vs custom SCR. JSON-Patch is standard but verbose; SCR is compact and easier to redact. Decision leaning toward SCR with optional JSON-Patch in evidence store for full fidelity. (See comment from design review below.)
2) How to represent batched role assignments (assign_role applied to 500 users) without overloading the log. Proposed: collapse to a single op with a count hint (e.g., "M|role.members|<hash>|<hash>|added-500-users").
3) Canonical actor naming for external idps: include both idp_id and external_subject; consider adding actor_affinity field for multi-tenant correlation.

Next steps / acceptance criteria:
- Finalize SCR encoding and publish spec doc + examples (this ticket)
- Implement emission library in control-plane (Go) and console (TS) with unit tests and roundtrip ingestion tests
- Add ingestion transforms to the analytics pipeline to index top changed_paths and outcome metrics
- Security review sign-off and a short runbook for evidence retrieval
